content.comment_body: Is anyone aware if [company_name] plans to release an update or service pack for compatibility with Vista for [product_name]? I managed to run the application on my system using Windows>Tools>Application>start.exe from the [product_name] CD (version 5). It works well until I try to upload or download a program. Has anyone been able to get further, specifically to successfully upload/download?

Hi [user_name], I can't check Vista since we don't use it. However, I've heard it should work, including upload/download operations. Try copying the executable folder from the [product_name] CD onto your computer. Right-click the application file, go to properties, and select the 'run in Windows XP Mode' option before launching it. Supposedly, this works. Also, I've heard [company_name] intends to release a Vista-compatible version by the end of summer 2007. I hope this helps! If possible, please share your results with the group. Regards

[user_name], that worked perfectly! I copied the folder from the CD (from windows/tools/applications) to my hard drive, then located [product_name].exe, right-clicked, and set compatibility to Windows XP or earlier. I also added a shortcut to my desktop. Thanks! The issue with Vista and [product_name] is that its installer (InstallAnywhere) isn't designed for Vista, whereas installation tools like InstallShield do work; I'm not sure why [company_name] chose otherwise for this software when other programs they make (like [product_name]) use InstallShield.

Hello, I followed your instructions for running [product_name] version 5 SP2 on Vista Business CZ 32bit, but I still have problems. When I start the application, it launches and then closes within seconds. Does anyone have suggestions? I'd appreciate any advice. Thank you!

Hi, You could try copying the entire CD to your hard drive, then navigate to \Windows\Tools\Application and run [product_name].exe. After starting the program, you can download the latest service pack that is compatible with Vista.

After copying the CD to my hard drive, I also had to switch my Windows display to 'Windows Classic' to view all the buttons during the installation. Running in Windows XP compatibility mode was also needed. Then I could start setup.exe as normal. After installation, I changed my display settings back. I used V5.0.22 and no update or patch was needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered major compatibility challenges installing and running [product_name] v5 on Windows Vista, mainly due to the installer not supporting Vista. Workarounds involved copying the files to the hard drive, running in Windows XP compatibility mode, and sometimes changing the display settings to 'Windows Classic' for installation. While these approaches resolved issues for some, others continued to face crashes or difficulties with program upload/download functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] to provide a Vista-ready update or service pack for [product_name] v5 to enable seamless installation and reliable operation on Windows Vista.
